analysis.statement:
Define `track_indicator(initial_ids, selected_index, operations)`.

The state is an ordered tab strip whose tabs have distinct signed 64-bit integer identifiers. At most one tab is selected; its zero-based position is the indicator index.

`initial_ids` is the initial order. If it is empty, `selected_index` is `-1`. Otherwise, `0 <= selected_index < len(initial_ids)`, and that position is initially selected.

Each element of `operations` is one of:

* `("insert", p, ids)`: `ids` is a nonempty sequence of identifiers that have never appeared before, even as removed tabs. Insert them in their given order immediately before position `p`, where `0 <= p <= current_length`. An existing selection remains attached to the same identifier. If the strip was empty, the first inserted identifier becomes selected.
* `("remove", ids)`: `ids` is a nonempty sequence of pairwise distinct identifiers, all currently present. Remove them simultaneously. If the selected identifier survives, it remains selected. time_memory_risks: numeric bounds too large for naive loops or arrays
n up to ~1e5–5e5; need near-linear work

plan.approach: Use a balanced binary search tree (treap) keyed by implicit position to support split/merge, reverse flag, and node removal by identifier. Maintain a dictionary mapping identifier to node. For each operation, perform splits/merges in O(log n). For remove, collect nodes, delete them, and adjust selection per rules. For reverse, apply lazy reverse on the split segment. Complexity per operation O(log n).
data_structures: treap node with fields: id, priority, size, left, right, rev flag
plan.complexity_target: O((n+m) log n) time, O(n) memory
traps_to_handle: simultaneous removal – delete all nodes before selection logic
large bounds – avoid full array materialization
plan.python_signature: def track_indicator(initial_ids: List[int], selected_index: int, operations: List[Tuple]) -> List[int]
test_ideas: 1. Simple insert and remove with selection change
2. Remove selected tab with right neighbor
3. Remove selected tab with no right neighbor but left neighbor
5. Reverse middle segment and check selection stays same
7. Large random sequence to test performance
